meta.title: The A Form: The Chord You Learned First
meta.summary: The A form of A minor is the open Am chord itself, and the single finger that turns open A into open Am is the chapter's whole rule under one hand.

spans.text: The A form of A minor is the open

Here's the one finger that gets you there. Open
. String 2 moves from fret 2 to fret 1. That's the chapter's whole rule, played out under a single finger: the
, and nothing else in the chord moves at all.
That's worth sitting with for a second, because it runs against how most players think about this chord. Open

usually gets filed as a beginner chord — the second or third thing anyone learns, before there's any system to put it in. It never stops being that. But it's also, at the same time, one-fifth of a map that covers the whole neck, sitting in the exact window CAGED would have put it in anyway. Nothing about learning the system changes the chord in your hand; it only changes what you know is next to it.
